summary: Turn the signed-in viewer's own Assistant's self-Map on or off
description: A narrow, session-bound route in the Duty Menu publish's shape (assistant-self-map ADR 0002). The body is one bit, `{ "on": true | false }` (Turn on and Update now send true, Turn off false); whose Assistant comes from the session (the Owner's is the instance TA; anyone else's their own), and nothing in the request can name another Assistant, choose an entry or pick a relay. Refused first: no session (401 not-signed-in), a body whose `on` is not a boolean (400 bad-request), no Assistant on this instance (403 no-assistant). One press at a time per Assistant. The press reads this instance's relay, its copy of the newest version a press here has seen or signed (kept on the data volume, so it survives a strfry wipe), and the outside relays together for the Assistant's kind 10040 (and, to turn on, the whole self-Map check); the newest wins. With no version on this instance's relay and no copy (an Assistant's first press here), the read finishes only when the Assistant's relay-list lookup finished (a list found nowhere counts only when every outside configured publish relay answered) and one of its write relays answered (or, having none, one of the other outside relays did, or there were none to ask). When a read does not finish, or the version found is not the Assistant's own validly signed one, it answers 503 not-read and changes nothing. It keeps the version found as the copy when newer (or in place of a copy that failed its check), then remembers the choice (assistant-self-map.json on the data volume), and publishes nothing when the self-entries found are already the target and this instance's relay holds that version and, when that target is not empty, no expiration or other owned tag sits beside them. Otherwise it signs a new kind 10040 whose self-entries are exactly what the self-Map should say (none, to turn off), keeping every other tag and the content as found (an expiration is dropped beside a self-entry), dated after the version it replaces, and keeps it as the copy; a removal retracts nothing. It is written to this instance's relay first (a failed write sends it nowhere), then, each once, to the relays its self-entries name and to at most 50 relays from events, each resolved first and never connected to unless public: the Assistant's write relays and the relays the found version's self-entries named. Local-only mode keeps it here. Nothing calls this when an Assistant is created or on a schedule.
